avoid_supplements.name: Potassium supplements
avoid_supplements.mechanism: ARBs increase renal potassium retention; combined supplementation elevates hyperkalemia risk
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated without physician oversight; monitor serum potassium if supplementation essential

avoid_supplements.name: NSAIDs (including supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: NSAIDs reduce antihypertensive efficacy and increase hyperkalemia and acute kidney injury risk with ARBs
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; use acetaminophen for pain management instead

avoid_supplements.name: ACE inhibitors
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Combined use increases hyperkalemia, hypotension, and renal dysfunction risk
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine; use either ARB or ACE inhibitor monotherapy

caution_supplements.name: Licorice root
caution_supplements.mechanism: May cause sodium retention and potassium loss, potentially counteracting antihypertensive effect
caution_supplements.action: Limit intake; monitor blood pressure if used

caution_supplements.name: Hawthorn
caution_supplements.action: Monitor blood pressure; report dizziness or syncope to physician

avoid_foods.name: High-potassium foods (excessive amounts)
avoid_foods.mechanism: ARBs reduce urinary potassium excretion; excessive dietary potassium increases hyperkalemia risk
avoid_foods.action: Consume potassium-rich foods (bananas, spinach, tomatoes) in moderation; do not restrict entirely without guidance

caution_foods.name: High-sodium foods
caution_foods.mechanism: Excessive sodium intake may attenuate antihypertensive efficacy of telmisartan
caution_foods.action: Encourage moderation of salt intake to optimize blood pressure control

caution_foods.name: Grapefruit juice
caution_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition may slightly increase telmisartan exposure
caution_foods.action: Occasional consumption likely safe; limit if concerned about increased bioavailability

monitoring_notes: Monitor serum potassium, creatinine, and blood pressure regularly, especially in patients with renal impairment or diabetes. Counsel on signs of hyperkalemia (weakness, palpitations) and acute kidney injury, and avoid NSAIDs and potassium supplements without explicit physician approval.
